restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

History, stated plainly (W.1): rule K reads no run outcome, but it was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, and its author knew their outcomes (R5 46/48 and R6 44/48 at K = 96; positive spaces per enumerated space 0.037 and 0.031, above the model's 0.0265; each 40/48 if truncated at 50 spaces; stage-2 maxima 308 and 315). Premise P is no longer used (proof Z.1): the algorithm reads the trail of proof 3 as advice. Its provenance: P's certified native run (D15, charged) certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P), with 7,251,935 matches; in every review the organizer recomputes the structural counts (r5-trail-0, 1, 23), the output core's level and its (core, beta2) against ALPHA3_BITS and BETA2 (r5-count-2 trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap (r5-count-2 trials 8, 9). Correctness of an output does not depend on the trail being optimal.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target and fixed advice (P's certified output). Success is measured end to end by R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F): rule K, plan, driver, analysis and every file hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run; 48 complete runs of v20 (K = 50; also complete runs of v22, X.11, and of v25, which starts from P's certified output exactly as every R7 run did, Z.1), all reported: 39 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.6956, so by the plan's rule 0.40 is claimed. B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted in R7 (largest attempt 197,334 work units, at most 310 stage-2 pairs, true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes. Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F) with the collisions of its first 15 successful runs as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 8 seed-picked R7 successes per review (one per stratum; v25s, Z.6); r5-bpfull runs a whole B' of an R7 run from its label, checks R7's table and bound and runs connector attempts with organizer coins; r5-count checks v25's counted multi-pass stage 1 and its block price (Z.3), T2 leaf and state step (Z.2), P's core-by-core driver on a sub-problem and its cap (W.4) and P's certifying level on the output core; r5-mitm-0, 1 check seed-picked cores, v25's half-vector step, per_a and match step with its unrolled run loop (Z.2); r5-trail-0, 1, 23 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v26's algorithm, which is v25's (v22's with P's certified output read as advice; proof Z.1) outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of the pre-registered study R7 are an unselected sample of v20's (equally v22's and v25's) runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R7 run is a complete run of v20 with label-derived coins (proof W.2): r7run.py makes algorithm()'s calls in algorithm()'s order from r5v20.py, which is v19's experiment file with K_SPACES = 50, A_ADV = 1067, A_MAX = 4268 and S2CAP = 2^11 (and an R5-replay bound written as 96); the shipped r5.py differs from it only in trail_search's loop order (W.4: same output, Lemma W; R7 uses P's certified output, as R5 and R6 did), in the organizer replay tables (W.10) and in the spacing of ten constant tables (AST-checked); v22's r5.py differs from v20's only in the counted programs and their checks (X), which algorithm() never calls, and in whitespace outside algorithm()'s call graph; v22's algorithm() and every definition it reaches are byte-identical to v20's (X.10, X.11); v25's algorithm() starts from P's certified output, exactly as every R7 run did, and by AST differs from v22's only there (Z.1); v25's counted programs (Z.2, Z.3) are not called by algorithm(). E on a space is fes (exact stage 1, Lemma 4, self-checked at 64 checkpoints) and stage 2 by complete digests in fes's order on at most S2CAP passes, which changes at most which colliding pair of a space is output. In R7, B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted: largest attempt 197,334 work units (X_MAX 2^20), stage-2 counts 199-310 (S2CAP 2^11), true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units (B_TRUE 2^29), at most 1,201 attempts in a run (A_MAX 4268); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes (per-run table, W.2). Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R7: 39 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.6956, so by R7's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. Premise R: rule K, R7's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, experiment file and enumerator were hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof W.2, Appendix F: per-run table and ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; which runs the organizer replays and which collisions are certificates was fixed before any result existed. The model that chose K predicts p_50 = 0.739; R7 measures the algorithm itself. Premise P is not used: the trail is advice whose construction D15 charges (Z.1); the organizer still re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R7: r5-R-0..7 re-derive 8 seed-picked R7 successes per review (one per stratum; v25s, Z.6) from their labels; r5-bpfull re-runs a whole B' of an R7 run; the first 15 R7 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R7's failures, run order and timing are logged by us. The organizer re-derives 16 of R7's 39 successes per review (run 22 only in the per-run ledger); failures are not re-run. Rule K was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, with their outcomes known (proof W.1); R7 ran after rule K and its plan were hashed. R5 and R6 (K = 96) are not runs of v20. The advice's full-scale certification rests on v15's native run, which D15 charges (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks the output core and seed-picked cores per review at the certifying level; success does not depend on it (Z.1).

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^30.6668 units; its B' runs at true cost and its E spaces at v25's counted E), v15's D15 at the counted prices of v25's programs (2^29.4371 units: the certified native T3 run of P, which alone constructed the advice, the T1/T2 run behind cores.bin, the Python T3 re-runs, stage-1 development and the driver self-test), v17's D16 (2^27, bound), D19 (2^28.7232), D20 (2^29.0730), v21's D21 (2^22.6078), D22 (2^26.7962), the peers' build checks of the programs v25 adopts (D_Y 2^14, D_v23 2^25, D_v24 2^24.53) and v25's D23 (2^26.8163, every run its author made for v25 except executions of the organizer's harness) and our D26 (2^20, stated bound) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v26's algorithm (v25's) reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. K, A_ADV, A_MAX and S2CAP come from rule K, an a-priori analysis hashed before the evidence run R7, so v14's pre-registration C (whose only role was keeping K = 96) fixes no number of v22 or v25. X_MAX and B_TRUE come from v13's run-free rule. Every other run produced program text, verified logged results, measured success under a pre-registered plan whose only outcome-dependent decision is whether its package is claimed (R5, R6, R7; for R7 the alternative was v19, a separate package, not another constant: W.3), re-derived logged computations (v17's B' re-derivations, V.5; executions of the organizer's harness, W.10, X.10) or fixed no number (A1: proof V.6). (v26, AA.2) v15's stopped contiguous-block T3 run, its six-layout comparison and their count-only measurements fixed only BLK, a constant of P. Since Y, P is not part of the algorithm, BLK is not reachable from algorithm() (AST), and by Lemma P the advice is identical for every block partition, so no outcome of those runs could change a number the algorithm reads. They are listed and not charged, like A1 (design work producing code that is charged when it runs) and item B (earlier runs that produced the same trail).
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^29.980777) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1, U.5, W.3, W.6 and X.8 list every run (v15's list, D16, the B' re-derivations of V.5, every run made for v19, v20, v22 and v25, with hashes; Z.4 lists D23). R7's plan would have fallen back to v19 on failure; a reader who charges R7 for that gets the R7 sensitivity above (W.3). D15's former largest item (v15's stopped run, charged complete in v25) is not charged in v26 (AA); D15 (v26) doubled 32.3983. D16 is v17's stated bound.
